source_groups.label: Animodar chapter begins below distinct divider; choose preceding syzygy
claims: heading
CHAP. XCIX. Of the Rectification of a Nativity by Animodar
New numbered natal chapter teaches Animodar birth-time rectification.
Printed XCIX corresponds to sequential/editorial C; it is not part of prior Trutine chapter.
context
Many and those very learned ... use
Lilly says numerous learned astrologers use Animodar to amend estimated natal time.
Practitioner prevalence claimed historically; no quantified sample or accuracy.
prerequisite
erected your Scheame ... estimative time
The student begins with a natal chart erected for the estimated birth time.
Uncorrected chart is the input; do not assume its clock or houses are accurate.
historical_attribution
Ptolomey directs
Lilly attributes the following syzygy selection procedure to Ptolemy.
Original Ptolemaic source parity is not independently authenticated by this batch.
condition
last new Moone ... before the Birth
If the preceding syzygy was a new Moon, examine its zodiacal sign and degree.
New-Moon path distinct from full-Moon path.
condition
if it was a full Moon
If the preceding syzygy was a full Moon, select the relevant luminary's zodiacal sign and degree.
Full Moon is an opposition; planet selection additionally depends on which light was above the horizon.
condition
either of the lights ... above the earth
For a preceding full Moon, examine the Sun or Moon that was above the earth at the opposition.
Horizon-based conditional criterion; no actual ephemeris calculated here.

source_groups.label: Choose essential-dignity winner and place Ascendant or Midheaven by proximity
claims: condition
Planet ... most dignities ... essential in that degree
Determine which natal planet possesses the most essential dignities at the chosen syzygy degree.
Rule depends on domicile/exaltation/triplicity/terms and a historical dignity table; score system not reproduced fully.
comparison
degrees he is in ... nearer ... cusp ascendant ... Mid-heaven
Compare the candidate planet's natal longitude with the degrees at the Ascendant and Midheaven cusps.
Must compare zodiacal circular angular distances, not the sheer raw numbers without wrap handling.
method
nearer ... cusp ascendant ... place so many degrees ascending
If the planet lies closer to the Ascendant, set the proposed ascending zodiacal degree equal to that planet's position.
Birth time must then be adjusted to reconstruct the stated Ascendant; not independently proven.
method
if ... nearer ... Mid-heaven then ... make degrees of Mid-heaven
If closer to the Midheaven, use the planet's natal zodiacal position as the corrected Midheaven.
Distinct output and house angle from the Ascendant branch.
method
vary your former figure according to either of those Angles
Recompute the estimated horoscope to satisfy the selected corrected cusp.
A deterministic reconstruction requirement once original ephemeris/method pinned.
condition
two Planets have equall dignities
If two planets tie in essential dignity at the degree, Lilly supplies a further criterion.
Tie resolution rather than independent confirmation.
condition
accept ... who is neerest in degrees to the Ascendant
Break an essential-dignity tie in favor of the planet nearer the Ascendant.
Source tie rule favors Ascendant; it does not prescribe an empirical statistical tie-break.
qualification
previously estimated and corrected chart may differ
This can change the estimated time or angle if the planet's natal placement differs from the initial cusp.
Direction and magnitude of actual clock shift remain dependent on chart reconstruction.

source_groups.label: Merchant merchant sample full Moon Sept 15 1616, daylight solar position and Saturn
claims: context
our Nativity was rectified by accidents
Lilly explicitly says this merchant's natal figure was already rectified from significant life events.
Animodar is being compared retrospectively against an accident-adjusted chart, not an independent truth.
authorial_outcome_claim
estimative time ... did not differ ... above one degree
He says the initially estimated time differed from his accident-rectified figure by no more than about one rising degree.
This is a claimed agreement between his own procedures, not actual independently recorded birth-time error.
example
15 September 1616 being Sunday
He dates the relevant preceding syzygy to Sunday 15 September 1616.
Source date; Julian-day and ephemeris parity not independently computed.
example
opposition Moon or full Moon foure dayes before birth
He specifies an opposition/full Moon four days before the merchant's September 19 birth.
The chosen full Moon is a retrospective lookup.
example
about eleven of clock day time
The example gives the preceding opposition's time at roughly 11 o'clock in daytime.
Historical clock/location ambiguity.
condition
Sun ... 2 degrees 32 minutes Libra ... above earth
At the full Moon, the Sun at about Libra 2°32′ was the luminary above the horizon, so Lilly selects that degree.
Source-specified luminary selection, not independently calculated syzygy data.
method
Table of Essential dignities page 104
He directs checking his dignity table at Libra 2°32′.
Points back to Book I source; table must be available to reproduce the dignity score.
condition
Saturn ... exaltation and triplicity ... terme
He claims Saturn is the principal dignity-holder there through exaltation, triplicity and term.
Specific traditional dignity predicates requiring source and chart-parity verification.
source_internal_judgement
Saturn ... principall ruler of that full Moon
Lilly selects Saturn as the Animodar planet for this syzygy.
Historical rule application, not observed correction outcome.

source_groups.label: Example corrected cusp, competing Venus and strong adverse assessment of precision
claims: example
we shall find him in 9 ...
Lilly describes Saturn's natal position as near nine degrees of a zodiacal sign in the merchant's source figure.
Original sign glyph needs deliberate standalone diplomatic confirmation; do not guess its label in this data row.
condition
neerer degree ascending then ... Mid-heaven
For Saturn, the comparison favors the estimated Ascendant rather than the Midheaven.
Original circular distances and timestamps have not been independently recomputed.
source_internal_result
Ascendant ... ninth of Capricorn and 2 min
He infers a corrected Ascendant near Capricorn 9°02′ from Saturn's position.
Source-asserted result, not a validated birth time.
authorial_qualification
had we accepted of Venus to have most dignities
He notes some astrologers could instead award Venus the most essential dignities.
Source explicitly acknowledges competing dignity attribution.
authorial_qualification
a strange concurrence
He suggests Venus would produce an intriguing agreement.
No specified independently authenticated truth criterion or supporting record.
authorial_assessment
neither Trutine of Hermes or this ... so sure foundation ... Accidents
He rates neither Animodar nor Trutine as well-founded as accident-based rectification.
Explicit negative comparative confidence, despite preceding worked illustration.
authorial_recommendation
Children ... before any accidents happen ... use this way and the other
When rectifying a child's chart before notable life events exist, he says the two preliminary syzygy/Trutine methods may still be used.
Pragmatic fallback, not an endorsement of proven future predictive validity.
